This present Suit is filed by the plaintiff against the defendants, declaring that the plaintiff is the lawful owner in possession and enjoyment of the schedule property, directing the defendants by way of mandatory injunction to demolish the O.S.No.1836/2004 structures put on the suit schedule property and further directing them to deliver vacant possession of the suit schedule property in favour of plaintiff, and for permanent injunction and such other consequential reliefs.
Schedule:
All that piece and parcel of the residential site bearing No.493, Intermediate/corner situated in Pattanagere village, Kengeri Hobli, Bangalore South Taluk, Kengeri Hobli,
Bangalore South Taluk, in private layout formed by the REMCO (BHEL) House Building Cooperative Society Limited, measuring 60 x 40 feet, bounded on the:
East by - Road, West by - Site Nos.501-500 North by - Site No.492, South by - Sy.No.494 2. The brief facts of the Plaintiff's case is as under- The plaintiff is the absolute owner in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property.

The then Sarakki Notified Area, now Rajarajeshwari Nagar City Municipal Council had issued a Khata endorsement on 5.9.1994 and also collected taxes continuously from 1994-95 up till date.
The Society had also acquired lands in Pattanagare Village in the year 1984-85 and after acquiring the same, it had submitted a layout plan to the Bangalore Development Authority for its approval

sentences.text: Thus, the Society had formed a layout in the lands that were acquired by it.
Since the plaintiff being one of the member of the 5th Defendant Society, the schedule site came to be allotted to him in the year 1989 and the possession was also delivered.

However, the documents of conveyance were came to be executed in the year 1992, the plaintiff continued to be in possession and enjoyment of the schedule site for the last 15 years as a rightful owner thereof.
Thus, the plaintiff has become the title owner in respect of the schedule site.

It appears there were some litigation between the Society and the erstwhile land owners and by virtue of the orders of the court,
it appears the 5th defendant Society has lost the legal battle.
But the fact remains that the plaintiff continued to be in possession of the schedule site for last 15 year without any let or hindrance O.S.No.1836/2004 whatsoever from quarters.

It appears the defendants I to 4 who are the L.R. of the erstwhile landlords, have also received compensation subsequent to the passing of the order by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India i.e., after 1995.

Thus, the defendants 1 to 4 relinquished all their rights, title and interest in respect of the schedule site and they cannot make use of the judgments rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in respect of the schedule site.

2(a). It is stated that the plaintiff who is an employee of the REMCO (BHEL) and being the member,
had invested his hard- earned money to have a residence in Bangalore City.

The plaintiff has also applied to the Rajarajeshwari Nagar CMC for approval of the building plan so as to construct the house on the Schedule site the plaintiff as an employee of the REMCO (BHEI) has invested his lifetime savings in order to acquire the schedule site.
The defendants 1 to 4 have no legal right whatsoever to interfere with the possession of the schedule site by the plaintiff.

By virtue of the orders of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, though there is no specific direction to the plaintiff or to the 5th defendant, the defendants 1 to 4 are demanding possession of the schedule site.

It is pertinent to state here that before rendering any judgment either by the Hon'ble High Court O.S.No.1836/2004 of Karnataka or by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, this plaintiff had acquired right, title and interest in respect of the schedule site and he is not a party in any of the proceedings that have between the defendants 1 to 4 and the 5th defendant.
Hence, any judgment passed is not binding on the plaintiff.
Therefore.
the defendants 1 to 4 have no legal right to dispossess the plaintiff from the schedule site.
During the pendency of the suit, the Defendants have trespassed into the suit schedule property and constructed building on the same without there being any legal right whatsoever.
The defendants are fully aware of the fact of pendency of the suit.
Despite the same, after service of summons by this Hon'ble Court, they have constructed a building and the same is completed in 2007 January.
When the plaintiff visited the suit schedule property in 2007, he found that the defendants have constructed a building in order to establish the right in respect of the suit schedule property.

Since the building is constructed during the pendency of the suit, it is just and necessary to direct the defendant to demolish the structures put up on the suit schedule property and deliver the same in favour of the plaintiff.

2(b). It is stated that, 5th defendant Society has filed a suit against the defendants seeking for declaration in O.S.No.1836/2004 0.S.No.16365/2005 and the defendants were represented by their GPA Holder in the said suit and accordingly, the said suit came to be decreed on 17.08.2005 granting declaration in favour of the 5th defendant-Society and its members,

Since the defendants are parties to the said proceedings, the constructions made by them on the suit schedule property is illegal and contrary to the decree passed in OS. No.16365/2005 and hence, this suit is also for a mandatory for demolition of the Ranganath S K vs Krishna on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142284764/
4 building
Constructed on the property.

As already stated above, the plaintiff has acquired right, and interest in the year 1989 itself and the documents execute in favour of the plaintiff only in the year 1992 prior to the Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and hence, the plaintiff has perfected his title to the schedule site by adverse possession and nobody can question the same much less the defendants l to 4.

However, the defendants 1 to 4 who are the L.Rs., of the erstwhile landlords, are trying to enter upon the schedule land and dispossess the plaintiff from the same forcibly and one such attempt was made on 4.2.2004 when the defendants 1 to 4 entered upon the schedule land along with their henchmen and tried to dispossess the plaintiff from the same.

However with great difficulty with the help of his friends and well-wishers, the O.S.No.1836/2004 plaintiff was able to resist the illegal and high-handed acts of the defendants 1 to 4 and their henchmen.
However.
The defendants 1 to 4 left the spot saying that they would come again with large men and materials so as to dispossess the plaintiff from the schedule land.

Immediately thereafter, the plaintiff approached the jurisdictional police, but the police declined to intervene in the matter and advised the plaintiff to approach the competent civil court as the dispute is of civil in nature.

As already stated above the plaintiff as acquired the title to the schedule site about 15 years back and remained in possession of the same for the last 15 years exercising the right of ownership in respect of the schedule site.

Even assuming or the sake of arguments that there is a judgment of the Honble Supreme Court of India to restore the land to the erstwhile landlords but there is no land available for restoration as the entire land is developed into a residential layout provided with all civic amenities and infact, a number of employees of REMCO (BHEL) and members of 5th defendant Society have constructed pucca RCC building by spending huge sums of money and as such, there is no land available for restoration.
Hence, prayed to decree the suit.
O.S.No.1836/2004 3. The defendant No.1 to 4 have filed their common written statement/counter claim.
They contend that the suit filed is the result of active collusion between the plaintiff and the defendant No.5 to defraud all of them.

After their late father Venkataramanappa died in 2002, they succeeded to the Sy.No.20/1 of Pattanagere village and since then they have been in possession and enjoyment of the said land measuring 1.04 acres including the suit site.
The alleged sale deed executed by defendant No.5 in favour of plaintiff and the alleged possessary right claimed by the plaintiff are denied.
They have been in possession and enjoyment of survey number land continuously.
The judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India reported in AIR 1995 SC 2263 is binding on the plaintiff also.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka quashed all the acquisition proceedings held in favour of defendant No.5 relating to Sy.No.20/1 of Pattanagere Panchayath.
The defendant No.5 did not acquire any right, title over an inch of land in Sy.No.20/1, even after SLP is filed by the defendant No.5 in the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
The suit descriptions are not affecting any of their property including Sy.No.20/1.

The Hon'ble Supreme court of India issued specific direction O.S.No.1836/2004 through the judgment reported in AIR 1995 SC 2235 that all the such lands shall be redelivered to the respective land owners and after such re-delivery of the said lands, subject to remitting of received compensation by the land owners, special re-delivery of the land.
The defendant No.5 have been harping upon the State Government not to issue said publication and to continued to play fraud on the land owners.
The plaintiff absolutely has not acquired title, interest or possessary right over any piece of suit property.

The identity of the suit site is also becomes Ranganath S K vs Krishna on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142284764/
5 important.

Hence, all of them pray for the relief of declaration of their title over Sy.No.20/1 with further declaration that the suit site is not at all in existence and thereafter to restrain the plaintiff from interfering into the suit site or the counter claim Sy.No.20/1.
Hence prayed to dismiss the suit of plaintiff and decree the counter claim.
4. The defendant No.6 appeared before the Court through his counsel and filed Counter Claim and Written statement.

The same is as under;
The present suit is only bereft of merits and same is liable to be dismissed.
The plaintiff is guilty of suppression of O.S.No.1836/2004 facts and misrepresentation and have not come before this Court with clean hands.

The plaintiff has concealed the fact that the Supreme Court of India have quashed the society for formation of the plaintiff's schedule property by stating that acquisition is illegal and also directed the said society to restore the land to the defendant No.1 to 4 family.
The plaintiff has conveniently concealed the fact that the plaint schedule property is not existed as on date of filing of the present suit. 4(a).

(b) It is stated that in the year 2013, the plaintiff tried to disturb the possession of this defendant,
after which the Defendant No.6 approached her Counsel regarding the same, wherein she came to know that without making her as necessary party, the Plaintiff have obtained the Exparte Judgment dated 27.02.2013, against the Respondent Nos.2 to 5 in O.S.No.1836/2004, on the file of the Hon'ble III Additional City Civil Judge, Bangalore (CCH-25).

knowing regarding Ex-parte judgment passed in O.S.No.1836/2004, the Defendant No.6 herein have preferred an Appeal before the Hon'ble High Court in RFA No.942/2013.

It is relevant to note that Hon'ble High Court after considering the merits in favour of the Defendant No.6, have allowed her to contest the suit and remanded the matter back to this Hon'ble Court, to dispose of the case within given time frame.
Subsequently, this Hon'ble Court have issued Summons to the Defendant No.6 Counsels to appear before it on 01.06.2023 and intimated to file necessary documents in support of her case.

That after receiving the summons from this Hon'ble Court, the Defendant No.6 herein have appeared and filed application Under Order 1 Rule 10 of the CPC r/w Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, to permit her to implead as Proposed Defendant No.6 in O.S.No.1836/2004.
Thereafter the Plaintiff have filed objection to the impleading application of the defendant No.6 herein.
After hearing, this Hon'ble Court, by its Order dated 07/07/2023 have rejected/dismissed the impleading application filed by the Defendant No.6.

Being aggrieved by the said Order dated 07/07/2023, the Writ Petition No.21635/2023 was preferred by the Defendant No.6 before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, wherein this Defendant was permitted to be impleded vide its Order dated 11.03.2024.

The plaintiff claims his alleged title, possession and interest over the imaginary plaint schedule property, which is part of O.S.No.1836/2004 Sy.No.20/1 of Pattanagere village by virtue of sale deed executed by defendant No.5.

The said act of the plaintiff is illegal and amounts to contempt of Court order, the land acquisitions proceedings by defendant No.5 with respect to Sy.No.20/1 of Pattanagere village were came to be set aside by the Hon'ble Supreme Court and the said Apex Court directed the defendant No.5 to restore lands that have been acquired by them from the defendant No.1 to 4, as the defendant No.5 have no right to acquire the land under the provisions of land acquisition act.
Hence, the claim of the plaintiff in the present suit with respect to the plaint schedule property is imaginary and the said property is not existed as on the date of filing of the present suit.
The plaintiff has claimed his title by way of an allotment made of REMO (BHEL) Society.
It is reiterated that the entire acquisition proceedings have been quashed by Apex Court and the lands have been returned to the land owners.

In perusance of the said order,
the REMCO society has also withdrawn the amount deposited by it with the land acquisition authority and has given up its claim over the land in pursuance of Supreme Court Order.
The plaintiff being one of the member of REMCOM Society is claiming his title under the REMCO society as an allottee of the suit schedule property.
